plausibility.summary: Hypsodont, flat cheek teeth with lateral grinding are a standard adaptation to abrasive, cellulose-rich and grit-laden plant food. Granivory on grass seeds and fruit pits (paja_dulce, velilla, perlilla, grama_de_ceniza) is a high-calorie primary-consumer strategy consistent with tight trophic transfer (D25) and summer-concentrated seed heads on the rain-shadow meadow (F18). Slightly higher gravity (F2) mildly favors robust jaws but is not the main driver.
fixes: Hypsodont, flat cheek teeth with lateral grinding are a standard adaptation to abrasive, cellulose-rich and grit-laden plant food. Slightly higher gravity (F2) mildly favors robust jaws but is not the main driver.

analogues.organism: Muroidea granivores (voles, pocket gophers) — hypsodont molars for grass and seed wear; kangaroo rats — seed specialists with cheek teeth adapted to hard seeds.
